subproblems.title: Change of variables for Hⁿ-integrals over blow-ups η_{y,r}(S)
subproblems.statement: Let Q, n ∈ ℕ, y ∈ ℝ^Q, r > 0, let S ⊆ ℝ^Q be an arbitrary set and g : ℝ^Q → ℝ an arbitrary function, and let η = η_{y,r}, η(x) = r⁻¹(x − y). Then ∫_{η(S)} g dHⁿ = (rⁿ)⁻¹ ∫_S g(η(x)) dHⁿ(x), where Hⁿ = μHE[n] on ℝ^Q and both sides are Bochner set integrals (no integrability or measurability assumption is made; the identity includes the case where both sides are 0 by non-integrability).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (Q n : ℕ) (y : Eucl Q) (r : ℝ) (S : Set (Eucl Q)) (g : Eucl Q → ℝ), 0 < r → ∫ z in Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.blowUpMap y r '' S, g z ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl Q)) = (r ^ n)⁻¹ * ∫ x in S, g (Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.blowUpMap y r x) ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl Q))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Conventions: ℝ^P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P) = Eucl P with norm |·|; Hⁿ = μHE[n] (Mathlib's Euclidean-normalized n-dimensional Hausdorff measure, = μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)); on ℝⁿ, Hⁿ = Lⁿ = volume (`EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume`). B̄_ρ(y) = closedBall y ρ. η_{y,λ}(x) = λ⁻¹(x − y) is `Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.blowUpMap y λ`. ∫_A f dHⁿ is the Bochner set integral (0 when f is not integrable on A); ∫⁻ is the [0,∞]-valued lintegral. 'T is the approximate tangent space of S at y' means `Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n S y T` (Simon Ch. 3, Def. 1.4): finrank T = n and ∫_{η_{y,λ}(S)} φ dHⁿ → ∫_T φ dHⁿ as λ → 0+ for every φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^Q, ℝ). `HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ y T` (Def. 1.7) means finrank T = n and ∫_{η_{y,λ}(M)} φ(z) θ(y + λz) dHⁿ(z) → θ(y) ∫_T φ dHⁿ as λ → 0+ for every φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^Q, ℝ).

This is item 0(d) of the parent proof (η_{y,r} is a similarity of ratio r⁻¹), proved for every g.

1. (η is a measurable equivalence.) Since r ≠ 0, η(x) = r⁻¹(x − y) has the inverse ψ(z) = y + r z. Both maps are continuous affine maps of ℝ^Q, so η is a homeomorphism and hence a measurable equivalence e : ℝ^Q ≃ᵐ ℝ^Q (Borel σ-algebra) with e = η and e⁻¹ = ψ. In particular η is a measurable embedding and η⁻¹(η(S)) = S for every set S.

2. (Push-forward of Hⁿ.) Put μ := μHE[n] on ℝ^Q. Claim: μ.map η = ENNReal.ofReal(rⁿ) • μ. Let B be a Borel set. Then (μ.map η)(B) = μ(η⁻¹(B)) = μ(ψ(B)), and ψ(B) = τ_y(r • B) where τ_y(z) = y + z. The translation τ_y is an isometry of ℝ^Q, so μ(τ_y(r • B)) = μ(r • B) (Mathlib `Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image`). Since r ≠ 0, μ(r • B) = ‖r‖₊ⁿ • μ(B) (`MeasureTheory.Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀`). As r > 0, ‖r‖₊ⁿ = rⁿ and its image in [0, ∞] is ENNReal.ofReal(rⁿ). Thus (μ.map η)(B) = ENNReal.ofReal(rⁿ) · μ(B) for every Borel B, and two measures agreeing on all Borel sets are equal. (Equivalently one may use `MeasureTheory.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_homothety_image`, since ψ is a homothety of ratio r composed with a translation.)

3. (Restriction.) For a measurable equivalence e and any set s (measurable or not), (μ.map e).restrict s = (μ.restrict (e⁻¹(s))).map e (`MeasurableEquiv.restrict_map`). Taking s := η(S) and using e⁻¹(η(S)) = S (step 1) and step 2:
 (μ.restrict S).map η = (μ.map η).restrict (η(S)) = (ENNReal.ofReal(rⁿ) • μ).restrict (η(S)) = ENNReal.ofReal(rⁿ) • (μ.restrict (η(S))) (`Measure.restrict_smul`).

4. (Integrals.) For a measurable embedding η and any measure ν, ∫ g d(ν.map η) = ∫ g(η(x)) dν(x) for every function g, integrable or not (`MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map`). With ν := μ.restrict S and step 3:
 ∫_S g(η(x)) dμ(x) = ∫ g d((μ.restrict S).map η) = ∫ g d(ENNReal.ofReal(rⁿ) • μ.restrict(η(S))) = (ENNReal.ofReal(rⁿ)).toReal · ∫_{η(S)} g dμ = rⁿ ∫_{η(S)} g dμ,
 using `integral_smul_measure` (valid for every g) and (ENNReal.ofReal(rⁿ)).toReal = rⁿ because rⁿ ≥ 0.

5. (Conclusion.) Since rⁿ > 0, multiplying by (rⁿ)⁻¹ gives ∫_{η(S)} g dHⁿ = (rⁿ)⁻¹ ∫_S g(η(x)) dHⁿ(x). ∎ (For n = 0 this reads ∫_{η(S)} g dH⁰ = ∫_S g∘η dH⁰, consistent with H⁰ = counting measure and η bijective.)
proof_key_steps: η = blowUpMap y r is a measurable equivalence of ℝ^Q with inverse z ↦ y + r z, so η⁻¹(η(S)) = S.
μHE[n].map η = ofReal(rⁿ) • μHE[n] by translation invariance (isometry) and euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀.
MeasurableEquiv.restrict_map gives (μ⌞S).map η = ofReal(rⁿ) • μ⌞η(S).
MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map and integral_smul_measure give ∫_S g∘η = rⁿ ∫_{η(S)} g for every g; divide by rⁿ > 0.

subproblems.title: The image of a C¹ antilipschitz chart is Borel and locally Hⁿ-finite
subproblems.statement: Let Φ : ℝⁿ → ℝ^Q be C¹, let Ω ⊆ ℝⁿ be open, and let c > 0 with c|w − w′| ≤ |Φ(w) − Φ(w′)| for all w, w′ ∈ Ω. Then Φ(Ω) is a Borel subset of ℝ^Q, and Hⁿ(Φ(Ω) ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^Q (Hⁿ = μHE[n] on ℝ^Q).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (Q n : ℕ) (Φ : Eucl n → Eucl Q) (Ω : Set (Eucl n)), IsOpen Ω → ContDiff ℝ 1 Φ → (∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ w ∈ Ω, ∀ w' ∈ Ω, c * ‖w - w'‖ ≤ ‖Φ w - Φ w'‖) → MeasurableSet (Φ '' Ω) ∧ ∀ K : Set (Eucl Q), IsCompact K → (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl Q)) (Φ '' Ω ∩ K) < ∞
subproblems.natural_proof:
Conventions: ℝ^P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P) = Eucl P with norm |·|; Hⁿ = μHE[n] (Mathlib's Euclidean-normalized n-dimensional Hausdorff measure, = μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)); on ℝⁿ, Hⁿ = Lⁿ = volume (`EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume`). B̄_ρ(y) = closedBall y ρ. η_{y,λ}(x) = λ⁻¹(x − y) is `Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.blowUpMap y λ`. ∫_A f dHⁿ is the Bochner set integral (0 when f is not integrable on A); ∫⁻ is the [0,∞]-valued lintegral. 'T is the approximate tangent space of S at y' means `Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n S y T` (Simon Ch. 3, Def. 1.4): finrank T = n and ∫_{η_{y,λ}(S)} φ dHⁿ → ∫_T φ dHⁿ as λ → 0+ for every φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^Q, ℝ). `HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ y T` (Def. 1.7) means finrank T = n and ∫_{η_{y,λ}(M)} φ(z) θ(y + λz) dHⁿ(z) → θ(y) ∫_T φ dHⁿ as λ → 0+ for every φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^Q, ℝ).

This is items 0(b) (measurability) and 0(c) (local finiteness) of the parent proof.

1. (Injectivity.) If w, w′ ∈ Ω and Φ(w) = Φ(w′), then c|w − w′| ≤ 0, so w = w′. Thus Φ is injective on Ω.

2. (Borel image.) Ω is open, hence Borel, in the Polish space ℝⁿ, and Φ is continuous (C¹) and injective on Ω. By the Lusin–Souslin theorem, the image of a Borel set under a map that is continuous and injective on it is Borel (Mathlib `MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn`). Hence Φ(Ω) is Borel. (Alternatively, avoiding Lusin–Souslin: Ω is the countable union of the compact closed balls with rational centres and radii contained in Ω, so Φ(Ω) is a countable union of compact, hence closed, sets. `MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn` lives in Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Constructions.Polish.Basic, which may need to be imported.)

3. (Localization.) Let K ⊆ ℝ^Q be compact. If Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(K) = ∅ then Φ(Ω) ∩ K = ∅ and Hⁿ(∅) = 0. Otherwise fix w₀ ∈ Ω with Φ(w₀) ∈ K and put D := diam K < ∞. For every v ∈ Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(K), c|v − w₀| ≤ |Φ(v) − Φ(w₀)| ≤ D, so v ∈ B̄ := B̄_{D/c}(w₀) ⊆ ℝⁿ. Every point of Φ(Ω) ∩ K is Φ(v) for such a v, so Φ(Ω) ∩ K ⊆ Φ(B̄).

4. (Lipschitz bound on B̄.) Φ is C¹, so v ↦ DΦ(v) is continuous and therefore bounded on the compact set B̄: there is Λ ∈ ℝ≥0 with ‖DΦ(v)‖ ≤ Λ for all v ∈ B̄. B̄ is convex, so by the mean value inequality Φ is Λ-Lipschitz on B̄ (Mathlib `Convex.lipschitzOnWith_of_nnnorm_fderiv_le`, using differentiability of Φ at every point).

5. (Hausdorff measure of the image.) For a map that is Λ-Lipschitz on B̄, μH[n](Φ(B̄)) ≤ Λⁿ · μH[n](B̄) (`LipschitzOnWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le` with dimension n ≥ 0). By definition μHE[n] = κ_n • μH[n] on every (e)metric space, with the same constant κ_n = addHaarScalarFactor(volume, μH[n]) ∈ (0, ∞) depending only on n (`euclideanHausdorffMeasure_def`). Multiplying by κ_n: Hⁿ(Φ(B̄)) ≤ Λⁿ · Hⁿ(B̄), where on the right Hⁿ = μHE[n] on ℝⁿ.

6. (Finiteness.) On ℝⁿ, μHE[n] equals Lebesgue measure (`EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume`), which is finite on the compact set B̄. Therefore Hⁿ(Φ(Ω) ∩ K) ≤ Hⁿ(Φ(B̄)) ≤ Λⁿ · Lⁿ(B̄) < ∞ (monotonicity of the outer measure Hⁿ). ∎
proof_key_steps: Antilipschitz ⇒ Φ injective on Ω; Lusin–Souslin (continuous injective image of the Borel set Ω) ⇒ Φ(Ω) Borel.
For compact K with Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(K) ≠ ∅, Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(K) lies in the closed ball B̄ of radius diam(K)/c about a point w₀ ∈ Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(K).
Φ is C¹, so it is Λ-Lipschitz on the convex compact ball B̄.
Hⁿ(Φ(Ω) ∩ K) ≤ Hⁿ(Φ(B̄)) ≤ Λⁿ Lⁿ(B̄) < ∞.

subproblems.title: Area formula for a C¹ antilipschitz chart against continuous compactly supported functions
subproblems.statement: Let Φ : ℝⁿ → ℝ^Q be C¹, Ω ⊆ ℝⁿ open, and c > 0 with c|w − w′| ≤ |Φ(w) − Φ(w′)| for all w, w′ ∈ Ω. For v ∈ ℝⁿ put JΦ(v) := √det(⟨DΦ(v)e_i, DΦ(v)e_j⟩)_{i,j<n}, where e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1 is the standard basis of ℝⁿ. Then for every continuous compactly supported h : ℝ^Q → ℝ, ∫_{Φ(Ω)} h dHⁿ = ∫_Ω JΦ(v) h(Φ(v)) dLⁿ(v) (Hⁿ = μHE[n] on ℝ^Q, Lⁿ = volume on ℝⁿ; Bochner set integrals).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (Q n : ℕ) (Φ : Eucl n → Eucl Q) (Ω : Set (Eucl n)), IsOpen Ω → ContDiff ℝ 1 Φ → (∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ w ∈ Ω, ∀ w' ∈ Ω, c * ‖w - w'‖ ≤ ‖Φ w - Φ w'‖) → ∀ h : Eucl Q → ℝ, Continuous h → HasCompactSupport h → ∫ x in Φ '' Ω, h x ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl Q)) = ∫ v in Ω, Real.sqrt (Matrix.of fun i j : Fin n => inner ℝ (fderiv ℝ Φ v (EuclideanSpace.single i 1)) (fderiv ℝ Φ v (EuclideanSpace.single j 1))).det * h (Φ v)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Conventions: ℝ^P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P) = Eucl P with norm |·|; Hⁿ = μHE[n] (Mathlib's Euclidean-normalized n-dimensional Hausdorff measure, = μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)); on ℝⁿ, Hⁿ = Lⁿ = volume (`EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume`). B̄_ρ(y) = closedBall y ρ. η_{y,λ}(x) = λ⁻¹(x − y) is `Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.blowUpMap y λ`. ∫_A f dHⁿ is the Bochner set integral (0 when f is not integrable on A); ∫⁻ is the [0,∞]-valued lintegral. 'T is the approximate tangent space of S at y' means `Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n S y T` (Simon Ch. 3, Def. 1.4): finrank T = n and ∫_{η_{y,λ}(S)} φ dHⁿ → ∫_T φ dHⁿ as λ → 0+ for every φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^Q, ℝ). `HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ y T` (Def. 1.7) means finrank T = n and ∫_{η_{y,λ}(M)} φ(z) θ(y + λz) dHⁿ(z) → θ(y) ∫_T φ dHⁿ as λ → 0+ for every φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^Q, ℝ).

This is the injective area formula used in item 0(e) of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 2, (3.1), (3.2), (3.5)), specialized to a C¹ antilipschitz chart and test functions h ∈ C_c.

1. (The Jacobian.) For a linear map L : ℝⁿ → ℝ^Q, Mathlib's LinearMap.normDet satisfies normDet(L) ≥ 0 and normDet(L)² = det of the Gram matrix (⟨L b_i, L b_j⟩)_{i,j} for any orthonormal basis b of ℝⁿ (`LinearMap.normDet_nonneg`, `LinearMap.normDet_sq_eq_det_gram`). Using the orthonormal basis `EuclideanSpace.basisFun`, whose vectors are e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1 (`EuclideanSpace.basisFun_apply`), we get √det(⟨Le_i, Le_j⟩) = √(normDet(L)²) = normDet(L). Hence JΦ(v) = normDet(DΦ(v)) ≥ 0 for every v; this is Simon's Jacobian √det(DΦ(v)*DΦ(v)). In SimonGMT notation (Poincare/SimonGMT/Chapter02/AreaDomain.lean) areaJacobianWithin Φ s v := normDet(fderivWithin ℝ Φ s v), and for s open and v ∈ s we have fderivWithin ℝ Φ s v = fderiv ℝ Φ v, so areaJacobianWithin Φ s v = JΦ(v).
 Moreover JΦ is continuous: v ↦ DΦ(v) is continuous because Φ is C¹; each Gram entry ⟨DΦ(v)e_i, DΦ(v)e_j⟩ is therefore continuous in v; the determinant is a polynomial in the entries (`Continuous.matrix_det`); and √ is continuous.

2. (Reduction to a bounded open set.) Let K := tsupport h, a compact set; h(z) ≠ 0 implies z ∈ K. If Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(K) = ∅, then h(Φ(v)) = 0 for all v ∈ Ω and h = 0 on Φ(Ω), so both sides are 0. Otherwise fix w₀ ∈ Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(K), let ρ := diam(K)/c + 1 and s := Ω ∩ B_ρ(w₀) (open ball), an open bounded set. For v ∈ Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(K), c|v − w₀| ≤ |Φ(v) − Φ(w₀)| ≤ diam K < cρ, so Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(K) ⊆ s. Consequently:
 (a) the integrand v ↦ JΦ(v)h(Φ(v)) vanishes on Ω ∖ s, so ∫_Ω JΦ(v)h(Φ(v)) dLⁿ = ∫_s JΦ(v)h(Φ(v)) dLⁿ;
 (b) Φ(Ω) ∩ K ⊆ Φ(s) ⊆ Φ(Ω), so h vanishes on Φ(Ω) ∖ Φ(s) and ∫_{Φ(Ω)} h dHⁿ = ∫_{Φ(s)} h dHⁿ. Here Φ(Ω) and Φ(s) are Borel by the Lusin–Souslin theorem (`MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn`; Φ is continuous and, by step 3, injective on Ω).

3. (Φ on s.) Φ is injective on Ω (if Φ(v) = Φ(v′) then c|v − v′| ≤ 0), hence on s. DΦ is continuous, hence bounded by some Λ ∈ ℝ≥0 on the compact convex set B̄_ρ(w₀) ⊇ s, so by the mean value inequality (`Convex.lipschitzOnWith_of_nnnorm_fderiv_le`) Φ is Λ-Lipschitz on B̄_ρ(w₀), in particular on s. Let J_max := max of JΦ on B̄_ρ(w₀) (continuous on a compact set). Also Lⁿ(s) < ∞, and Hⁿ(Φ(s)) ≤ Λⁿ Lⁿ(B̄_ρ(w₀)) < ∞ (`LipschitzOnWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le`, μHE[n] = κ_n • μH[n], and μHE[n] = Lⁿ on ℝⁿ).

4. (Injective weighted area formula.) SimonGMT `Chapter02.weighted_area_formula_lipschitzOn_fiberSum` (Simon Ch. 2, 3.2 and 3.5): if s ⊆ ℝⁿ is Lebesgue measurable, Φ is Lipschitz on s and ω : ℝⁿ → [0, ∞] is a.e.-measurable for Lⁿ⌞s, then
 ∫⁻ (∑_{x ∈ s, Φ(x) = z} ω(x)) dHⁿ(z) = ∫⁻_s ofReal(areaJacobianWithin Φ s x) · ω(x) dLⁿ(x),
 where the fibre sum is `weightedAreaFiberSum s Φ ω z` and Hⁿ = μHE[finrank ℝ ℝⁿ] = μHE[n]. Because Φ is injective on s, the fibre {x ∈ s : Φ(x) = z} has at most one element: the fibre sum equals ω(x_z) if z = Φ(x_z) with x_z ∈ s, and 0 if z ∉ Φ(s). Write h⁺ := max(h, 0), h⁻ := max(−h, 0) (continuous, compactly supported, ≥ 0) and apply the formula with ω := ofReal ∘ h⁺ ∘ Φ, resp. ω := ofReal ∘ h⁻ ∘ Φ (continuous, hence measurable). The fibre sum becomes the indicator of Φ(s) applied to ofReal ∘ h^±, and with step 1 (areaJacobianWithin Φ s = JΦ on s) we obtain
 ∫⁻_{Φ(s)} ofReal(h^±(z)) dHⁿ(z) = ∫⁻_s ofReal(JΦ(v)) · ofReal(h^±(Φ(v))) dLⁿ(v) = ∫⁻_s ofReal(JΦ(v)h^±(Φ(v))) dLⁿ(v).

5. (Finiteness and the signed identity.) The right-hand sides are ≤ J_max · sup|h| · Lⁿ(s) < ∞, so both identities are between finite numbers. Since h is continuous, bounded, and Hⁿ(Φ(s)) < ∞, h is Hⁿ-integrable on Φ(s); since JΦ·(h∘Φ) is continuous and bounded on s and Lⁿ(s) < ∞, it is Lⁿ-integrable on s. Because JΦ ≥ 0, the positive and negative parts of JΦ·(h∘Φ) are JΦ·(h⁺∘Φ) and JΦ·(h⁻∘Φ). Writing each Bochner integral as the difference of the lintegrals of the positive and negative parts (`integral_eq_lintegral_pos_part_sub_lintegral_neg_part`) and subtracting the two identities of step 4 gives ∫_{Φ(s)} h dHⁿ = ∫_s JΦ(v)h(Φ(v)) dLⁿ(v).

6. (Conclusion.) Combining with step 2(a),(b): ∫_{Φ(Ω)} h dHⁿ = ∫_{Φ(s)} h dHⁿ = ∫_s JΦ·(h∘Φ) dLⁿ = ∫_Ω JΦ(v)h(Φ(v)) dLⁿ(v), where Lⁿ is `volume` on EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n). ∎ (For n = 0: ℝ⁰ is a point, the empty Gram determinant is 1, H⁰ is counting measure and L⁰ the unit point mass, and the identity reads h(Φ(0)) = h(Φ(0)) or 0 = 0; the argument above covers this case. No case distinction between n ≤ Q and n > Q is needed.)

Reduce to the bounded open set s = Ω ∩ B(w₀, diam(tsupport h)/c + 1), which contains Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(tsupport h); Φ is injective and Lipschitz on s.
Apply the injective weighted area formula (SimonGMT weighted_area_formula_lipschitzOn_fiberSum) with weights ofReal(h^±∘Φ); injectivity turns the fibre sum into the indicator of Φ(s).
All quantities are finite; subtract positive and negative parts and extend from s, Φ(s) back to Ω, Φ(Ω).

subproblems.title: A C¹ antilipschitz chart image has approximate tangent space DΦ(w)(ℝⁿ) at Φ(w)
subproblems.statement: Let Φ : ℝⁿ → ℝ^Q be C¹, Ω ⊆ ℝⁿ open, c > 0 with c|w − w′| ≤ |Φ(w) − Φ(w′)| for all w, w′ ∈ Ω, and w ∈ Ω. Then T := DΦ(w)(ℝⁿ) = LinearMap.range (fderiv ℝ Φ w) is the (unweighted, Simon Ch. 3 Def. 1.4) approximate tangent space of N := Φ(Ω) at y := Φ(w): finrank T = n and lim_{λ↓0} ∫_{η_{y,λ}(N)} φ dHⁿ = ∫_T φ dHⁿ for every φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^Q, ℝ).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (Q n : ℕ) (Φ : Eucl n → Eucl Q) (Ω : Set (Eucl n)), IsOpen Ω → ContDiff ℝ 1 Φ → (∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ w ∈ Ω, ∀ w' ∈ Ω, c * ‖w - w'‖ ≤ ‖Φ w - Φ w'‖) → ∀ w ∈ Ω, Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (Φ '' Ω) (Φ w) (LinearMap.range (fderiv ℝ Φ w).toLinearMap)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Conventions: ℝ^P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P) = Eucl P with norm |·|; Hⁿ = μHE[n] (Mathlib's Euclidean-normalized n-dimensional Hausdorff measure, = μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)); on ℝⁿ, Hⁿ = Lⁿ = volume (`EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume`). B̄_ρ(y) = closedBall y ρ. η_{y,λ}(x) = λ⁻¹(x − y) is `Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.blowUpMap y λ`. ∫_A f dHⁿ is the Bochner set integral (0 when f is not integrable on A); ∫⁻ is the [0,∞]-valued lintegral. 'T is the approximate tangent space of S at y' means `Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n S y T` (Simon Ch. 3, Def. 1.4): finrank T = n and ∫_{η_{y,λ}(S)} φ dHⁿ → ∫_T φ dHⁿ as λ → 0+ for every φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^Q, ℝ). `HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ y T` (Def. 1.7) means finrank T = n and ∫_{η_{y,λ}(M)} φ(z) θ(y + λz) dHⁿ(z) → θ(y) ∫_T φ dHⁿ as λ → 0+ for every φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^Q, ℝ).

This is items 0(a) and 0(e) of the parent proof (Simon: "since x ∈ N_j and N_j is a C¹ submanifold, lim ∫_{η(N_j)} f = ∫_{T N_j} f"). It uses the sibling results
 (BLOWUP) for y′ ∈ ℝ^P, r > 0, any S ⊆ ℝ^P and any g : ℝ^P → ℝ: ∫_{η_{y′,r}(S)} g dHⁿ = (rⁿ)⁻¹ ∫_S g(η_{y′,r}(x)) dHⁿ(x) (stated for every ambient dimension P; used with P = Q and with P = n);
 (AREA) for a C¹ map Ψ : ℝⁿ → ℝ^Q that is c′-antilipschitz on an open set U and every continuous compactly supported h: ∫_{Ψ(U)} h dHⁿ = ∫_U JΨ(v) h(Ψ(v)) dLⁿ(v), with JΨ(v) = √det(⟨DΨ(v)e_i, DΨ(v)e_j⟩).
Notation: L := DΦ(w) = fderiv ℝ Φ w, JΦ as in (AREA), N := Φ(Ω), y := Φ(w), T := range L.

1. (Lower bound for L; dimension.) Let s ∈ ℝⁿ. As Ω is open there is t₀ > 0 with w + ts ∈ Ω for 0 < t < t₀, and the antilipschitz hypothesis gives c t|s| ≤ |Φ(w + ts) − Φ(w)|, i.e. c|s| ≤ |t⁻¹(Φ(w + ts) − Φ(w))| for 0 < t < t₀. By the chain rule t ↦ Φ(w + ts) has derivative Ls at t = 0, so t⁻¹(Φ(w + ts) − Φ(w)) → Ls as t → 0+ (`HasDerivAt.tendsto_slope_zero_right`), and passing to the limit c|s| ≤ |Ls|. Hence L is injective, and finrank T = finrank ℝⁿ = n (`LinearMap.finrank_range_of_inj`). Also c|s − s′| ≤ |L s − L s′| for all s, s′ ∈ ℝⁿ, i.e. L is c-antilipschitz on ℝⁿ.

2. (Continuity of JΦ.) v ↦ DΦ(v) is continuous (Φ is C¹), so the Gram entries ⟨DΦ(v)e_i, DΦ(v)e_j⟩ are continuous, det is a polynomial in them (`Continuous.matrix_det`), and √ is continuous: JΦ is continuous and ≥ 0.

3. (Rewriting the blow-up integral.) Fix φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^Q, ℝ); choose R > 0 with tsupport φ ⊆ B̄_R(0) and put A := sup|φ|. For λ > 0 let η := η_{y,λ} on ℝ^Q and ζ := η_{w,λ} on ℝⁿ (ζ(v) = λ⁻¹(v − w)); both are homeomorphisms, so ζ(Ω) is open. Put I(λ) := ∫_{η(N)} φ dHⁿ.
 (a) By (BLOWUP) on ℝ^Q: I(λ) = (λⁿ)⁻¹ ∫_N φ(η(x)) dHⁿ(x).
 (b) h := φ∘η is continuous, and tsupport h = η⁻¹(tsupport φ) is compact, so by (AREA) with Ψ = Φ, U = Ω: ∫_N φ∘η dHⁿ = ∫_Ω JΦ(v) φ(η(Φ(v))) dLⁿ(v).
 (c) Let G_λ(s) := JΦ(w + λs) · φ(η(Φ(w + λs))) on ℝⁿ. By (BLOWUP) on ℝⁿ (base point w, ratio λ, S = Ω) together with μHE[n] = Lⁿ on ℝⁿ: ∫_{ζ(Ω)} G_λ dLⁿ = (λⁿ)⁻¹ ∫_Ω G_λ(ζ(v)) dLⁿ(v) = (λⁿ)⁻¹ ∫_Ω JΦ(v) φ(η(Φ(v))) dLⁿ(v), because w + λζ(v) = v.
 From (a)–(c), I(λ) = ∫_{ζ(Ω)} G_λ dLⁿ = ∫_{ℝⁿ} F_λ dLⁿ with F_λ := 1_{ζ(Ω)} · G_λ (`integral_indicator`, ζ(Ω) open), and η(Φ(w + λs)) = λ⁻¹(Φ(w + λs) − Φ(w)).

4. (Domination.) Let J_max := max{JΦ(z) : |z − w| ≤ R/c} (continuous function on a compact ball). Let 0 < λ ≤ 1 and s ∈ ℝⁿ with F_λ(s) ≠ 0. Then w + λs ∈ Ω (as s ∈ ζ(Ω)) and φ(λ⁻¹(Φ(w + λs) − Φ(w))) ≠ 0, so |Φ(w + λs) − Φ(w)| ≤ λR; by the antilipschitz bound for w, w + λs ∈ Ω, cλ|s| ≤ λR, i.e. |s| ≤ R/c; then |(w + λs) − w| = λ|s| ≤ R/c, so JΦ(w + λs) ≤ J_max. Hence |F_λ(s)| ≤ A · J_max · 1_{B̄_{R/c}(0)}(s) for all s ∈ ℝⁿ and all λ ∈ (0, 1]; this bound is Lⁿ-integrable and independent of λ. Each F_λ is measurable (indicator of an open set times a continuous function).

5. (Pointwise limit.) Fix s ∈ ℝⁿ and let λ → 0+. (i) w + λs → w ∈ Ω with Ω open, so eventually w + λs ∈ Ω, i.e. s = ζ(w + λs) ∈ ζ(Ω) and 1_{ζ(Ω)}(s) = 1. (ii) λ⁻¹(Φ(w + λs) − Φ(w)) → Ls (step 1), so φ(λ⁻¹(Φ(w + λs) − Φ(w))) → φ(Ls) by continuity of φ. (iii) JΦ(w + λs) → JΦ(w) by step 2. Hence F_λ(s) → JΦ(w) φ(Ls).

6. (Dominated convergence.) The filter 𝓝[>]0 is countably generated and the bound of step 4 holds for λ in the 𝓝[>]0-neighbourhood (0, 1]; by dominated convergence (`tendsto_integral_filter_of_dominated_convergence`), I(λ) = ∫ F_λ dLⁿ → ∫_{ℝⁿ} JΦ(w) φ(Ls) dLⁿ(s) as λ → 0+.

7. (Linear area formula.) Apply (AREA) to Ψ := L (a continuous linear map, hence C¹, with fderiv ℝ L v = L for every v — `ContinuousLinearMap.fderiv`), U := ℝⁿ (open) and the constant c (step 1), with h := φ: ∫_{L(ℝⁿ)} φ dHⁿ = ∫_{ℝⁿ} √det(⟨Le_i, Le_j⟩) φ(Ls) dLⁿ(s) = ∫_{ℝⁿ} JΦ(w) φ(Ls) dLⁿ(s), since DΦ(w) = L. As sets, L(ℝⁿ) = range L = T.

8. (Conclusion.) By steps 6 and 7, lim_{λ↓0} ∫_{η_{y,λ}(Φ(Ω))} φ dHⁿ = ∫_T φ dHⁿ for every φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^Q, ℝ); with finrank T = n (step 1) this is HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (Φ(Ω)) (Φ(w)) (LinearMap.range (fderiv ℝ Φ w)). ∎ (For n = 0, ℝ⁰ = {0}, Ω = {0}, N = {y}, T = {0}, and both sides equal φ(0); the argument covers this case.)
proof_key_steps: Antilipschitz + differentiability: c|s| ≤ |DΦ(w)s|, so DΦ(w) is injective and finrank T = n; DΦ(w) is c-antilipschitz on ℝⁿ.
JΦ(v) = √det Gram(DΦ(v)e_i) is continuous.
BLOWUP on ℝ^Q, AREA for Φ on Ω, and BLOWUP on ℝⁿ (substitution v = w + λs) give I(λ) = ∫ 1_{η_{w,λ}(Ω)}(s) JΦ(w+λs) φ(λ⁻¹(Φ(w+λs) − Φ(w))) ds.
Antilipschitz bounds the integrand by sup|φ| · max_{B̄_{R/c}(w)} JΦ · 1_{B̄_{R/c}(0)} for λ ≤ 1; pointwise limit JΦ(w) φ(DΦ(w)s).
Dominated convergence along 𝓝[>]0, then AREA for the linear map DΦ(w) on ℝⁿ identifies the limit with ∫_T φ dHⁿ.

subproblems.title: Lusin decomposition of (M, θ) into compact pieces with continuous weight (Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.8(1))
subproblems.statement: Let V ⊆ ℝ^Q be open, M ⊆ V Hⁿ-null-measurable, θ : ℝ^Q → ℝ with θ > 0 on M and θ Hⁿ-integrable on M ∩ K for every compact K ⊆ V. Then there are sets C_k ⊆ ℝ^Q (k ∈ ℕ) such that each C_k is compact, C_k ⊆ M, θ|C_k is continuous, Hⁿ(C_k) < ∞, and Hⁿ(M ∖ ⋃_k C_k) = 0.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (Q n : ℕ) (V M : Set (Eucl Q)) (θ : Eucl Q → ℝ), IsOpen V → M ⊆ V → NullMeasurableSet M (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl Q)) → (∀ y ∈ M, 0 < θ y) → (∀ K : Set (Eucl Q), IsCompact K → K ⊆ V → IntegrableOn θ (M ∩ K) (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl Q))) → ∃ C : ℕ → Set (Eucl Q), (∀ k, IsCompact (C k)) ∧ (∀ k, C k ⊆ M) ∧ (∀ k, ContinuousOn θ (C k)) ∧ (∀ k, (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl Q)) (C k) < ∞) ∧ (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl Q)) (M \ ⋃ k, C k) = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Conventions: ℝ^P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P) = Eucl P with norm |·|; Hⁿ = μHE[n] (Mathlib's Euclidean-normalized n-dimensional Hausdorff measure, = μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)); on ℝⁿ, Hⁿ = Lⁿ = volume (`EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume`). B̄_ρ(y) = closedBall y ρ. η_{y,λ}(x) = λ⁻¹(x − y) is `Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.blowUpMap y λ`. ∫_A f dHⁿ is the Bochner set integral (0 when f is not integrable on A); ∫⁻ is the [0,∞]-valued lintegral. 'T is the approximate tangent space of S at y' means `Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n S y T` (Simon Ch. 3, Def. 1.4): finrank T = n and ∫_{η_{y,λ}(S)} φ dHⁿ → ∫_T φ dHⁿ as λ → 0+ for every φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^Q, ℝ). `HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ y T` (Def. 1.7) means finrank T = n and ∫_{η_{y,λ}(M)} φ(z) θ(y + λz) dHⁿ(z) → θ(y) ∫_T φ dHⁿ as λ → 0+ for every φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^Q, ℝ).

This is step 1 of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.8(1): "by Lusin's Theorem 1.17 of Ch. 1, there is an increasing sequence {M_j} of compact subsets of M with Hⁿ(M ∖ ∪M_j) = 0 and θ|M_j continuous (hence has a positive lower bound, hence Hⁿ(M_j) < ∞)"). Let μ := μHE[n] on ℝ^Q.

1. (Countable compact cover of V.) Let D ⊆ ℝ^Q be a countable dense set (`TopologicalSpace.exists_countable_dense`). Let 𝒦 be the countable family of closed balls B̄_t(q) with q ∈ D, t ∈ ℚ, t > 0 and B̄_t(q) ⊆ V. Each member is compact (closed and bounded in ℝ^Q) and contained in V. Every x ∈ V lies in some member: V is open, so there is a rational t > 0 with B̄_{2t}(x) ⊆ V; pick q ∈ D with |q − x| < t; then x ∈ B̄_t(q) ⊆ B̄_{2t}(x) ⊆ V. If 𝒦 = ∅ then V = ∅ = M and C_k := ∅ works; otherwise enumerate 𝒦 = {K_i : i ∈ ℕ}. Then V = ⋃_i K_i, so M = ⋃_i M_i with M_i := M ∩ K_i.

2. (A Borel core of M_i on which θ is Borel.) Fix i. By hypothesis θ is μ-integrable on M_i; in particular θ is a.e.-strongly measurable for μ⌞M_i, so there are a Borel function θ̃_i : ℝ^Q → ℝ and a Borel set Z_i with μ(Z_i ∩ M_i) = 0 such that θ = θ̃_i on M_i ∖ Z_i. Since M and K_i are μ-null-measurable, so is M_i, hence there is a Borel set B_i⁰ ⊆ M_i with μ(M_i ∖ B_i⁰) = 0 (`NullMeasurableSet.exists_measurable_subset_ae_eq`). Put B_i := B_i⁰ ∖ Z_i: B_i is Borel, B_i ⊆ M_i, μ(M_i ∖ B_i) ≤ μ(M_i ∖ B_i⁰) + μ(M_i ∩ Z_i) = 0, and θ = θ̃_i on B_i.

3. (A finite Borel measure.) Let ν_i := (μ⌞B_i).withDensity(ofReal ∘ θ̃_i), so ν_i(E) = ∫⁻_{B_i ∩ E} ofReal(θ̃_i) dμ for Borel E (`withDensity_apply`, `Measure.restrict_restrict`). Then ν_i(ℝ^Q) = ∫⁻_{B_i} ofReal(θ) dμ ≤ ∫⁻_{M_i} ‖θ‖ₑ dμ < ∞. A finite Borel measure on a metric space is weakly regular (`Measure.WeaklyRegular.of_pseudoMetrizableSpace_of_isFiniteMeasure`), so for every Borel E with ν_i(E) < ∞ and every δ > 0 there is a closed F ⊆ E with ν_i(E ∖ F) < δ (`MeasurableSet.exists_isClosed_sdiff_lt`).

4. (Lusin.) Lusin's theorem (Simon Ch. 1, 1.17; SimonGMT `Chapter01.exists_isClosed_continuousOn_of_measurable`, Poincare/SimonGMT/Chapter01/Lusin.lean), applied to ν_i with the regularity of step 3, the Borel set B_i (ν_i(B_i) < ∞), the Borel function θ̃_i and ε := 1/(j + 1) (j ∈ ℕ), yields closed sets F_{i,j} ⊆ B_i with ν_i(B_i ∖ F_{i,j}) < 1/(j + 1) and θ̃_i|F_{i,j} continuous. As θ = θ̃_i on B_i ⊇ F_{i,j}, θ|F_{i,j} is continuous (`ContinuousOn.congr`). F_{i,j} is closed and contained in the compact set K_i, hence compact; and F_{i,j} ⊆ B_i ⊆ M.

5. (Finite measure of the pieces.) If F_{i,j} ≠ ∅, the continuous function θ attains its minimum m on the compact set F_{i,j} (`IsCompact.exists_isMinOn`), and m > 0 because F_{i,j} ⊆ M. Then m · μ(F_{i,j}) ≤ ∫⁻_{F_{i,j}} ofReal(θ) dμ ≤ ∫⁻_{M_i} ‖θ‖ₑ dμ < ∞, so μ(F_{i,j}) < ∞. If F_{i,j} = ∅, μ(F_{i,j}) = 0.

6. (Null remainder.) G_i := B_i ∖ ⋃_j F_{i,j} is Borel and ν_i(G_i) ≤ ν_i(B_i ∖ F_{i,j}) < 1/(j + 1) for every j, so ν_i(G_i) = ∫⁻_{G_i} ofReal(θ̃_i) dμ = 0. The integrand ofReal ∘ θ̃_i is measurable, and on G_i ⊆ B_i ⊆ M it equals ofReal(θ) > 0; by `lintegral_eq_zero_iff` it vanishes μ⌞G_i-a.e., which forces μ(G_i) = 0. Therefore μ(M_i ∖ ⋃_j F_{i,j}) ≤ μ(M_i ∖ B_i) + μ(G_i) = 0.

7. (Enumeration.) Let (C_k)_{k∈ℕ} enumerate the countable family (F_{i,j})_{i,j∈ℕ}, e.g. C_k := F_{(Nat.unpair k).1,(Nat.unpair k).2}. Each C_k is compact, C_k ⊆ M, θ|C_k is continuous (ContinuousOn θ C_k) and μ(C_k) < ∞ (steps 4, 5). Since M = ⋃_i M_i, M ∖ ⋃_k C_k ⊆ ⋃_i (M_i ∖ ⋃_j F_{i,j}), a countable union of μ-null sets (step 6); hence μ(M ∖ ⋃_k C_k) = 0. ∎

Lean note: `exists_isClosed_continuousOn_of_measurable` lives in Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter01.Lusin, which the frozen Contract does not import; import it where this lemma is proved and re-check that the frozen statement still elaborates unchanged.
proof_key_steps: Cover V by countably many compact closed balls K_i ⊆ V (rational radii, centres in a countable dense set).
On M_i = M ∩ K_i pick a Borel B_i ⊆ M_i of full measure on which θ equals a Borel function θ̃_i.

ν_i = θ̃_i·Hⁿ⌞B_i is a finite weakly regular Borel measure; Lusin (SimonGMT Chapter01.exists_isClosed_continuousOn_of_measurable) gives closed F_{i,j} ⊆ B_i with ν_i(B_i∖F_{i,j}) < 1/(j+1) and θ continuous on F_{i,j}; F_{i,j} ⊆ K_i is compact.
min θ > 0 on F_{i,j} and ∫_{M_i} θ < ∞ give Hⁿ(F_{i,j}) < ∞; ν_i(B_i∖⋃_j F_{i,j}) = 0 and θ > 0 give Hⁿ(M_i∖⋃_j F_{i,j}) = 0.

subproblems.title: Zero n-density of a locally finite weighted measure off its carrier (Upper Density Theorem)

'T is the approximate tangent space of S at y' means `Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n S y T` (Simon Ch. 3, Def. 1.4): finrank T = n and ∫_{η_{y,λ}(S)} φ dHⁿ → ∫_T φ dHⁿ as λ → 0+ for every φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^Q, ℝ). `HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ y T` (Def. 1.7) means finrank T = n and ∫_{η_{y,λ}(M)} φ(z) θ(y + λz) dHⁿ(z) → θ(y) ∫_T φ dHⁿ as λ → 0+ for every φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^Q, ℝ).

This is item 0(f) of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 1, Theorem 3.6, Upper Density Theorem), in the localized form used in steps 2(i), 2(ii) and 3 of the parent proof. Let μ := μHE[n] on ℝ^Q.

1. (The measure ν.) Let ν := (μ⌞S).withDensity(g), a Borel measure on ℝ^Q (no measurability of g or S is needed to form it). For every Borel set E, ν(E) = ∫⁻_E g d(μ⌞S) = ∫⁻_{S ∩ E} g dμ (`withDensity_apply`, `Measure.restrict_restrict`). In particular ν(B̄_ρ(y)) = ∫⁻_{S ∩ B̄_ρ(y)} g dμ for all y, ρ, and ν(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ W.

2. (Measurable hull.) Since S is μ-null-measurable there is a Borel set S′ ⊇ S with μ(S′ ∖ S) = 0 (e.g. S′ := toMeasurable μ S). ν is concentrated on S′: if E is Borel with E ∩ S′ = ∅ then S ∩ E = ∅, so ν(E) = 0; hence ν(E) = ν(E ∩ S′) for every Borel E.

3. (Countable compact family.) Let D ⊆ ℝ^Q be countable and dense, and 𝒦 the countable family of closed balls B̄_{2t}(q) ⊆ W with q ∈ D and t ∈ ℚ, t > 0. Every y ∈ W lies in the interior of some K ∈ 𝒦: choose rational t > 0 with B̄_{3t}(y) ⊆ W and q ∈ D with |q − y| < t; then y ∈ B_{2t}(q) ⊆ interior B̄_{2t}(q) and B̄_{2t}(q) ⊆ B̄_{3t}(y) ⊆ W. Each K ∈ 𝒦 is compact and K ⊆ W, so ν(K) < ∞.

4. (Upper Density Theorem.) ν̂ := ν.toOuterMeasure is Borel regular in Simon's sense (SimonGMT `Chapter01.measure_toOuterMeasure_isBorelRegular`). For K ∈ 𝒦 the set A_K := S′ ∩ K is Borel, hence ν̂-Carathéodory measurable, and ν̂(A_K) ≤ ν(K) < ∞. Simon Ch. 1, 3.6 (SimonGMT `Chapter01.simon_theorem_3_6`, or its a.e. form `Chapter01.ae_dimensionalUpperDensity_eq_zero_outside`, Poincare/SimonGMT/Chapter01/DensityComparison.lean, with real dimension n ≥ 0) states that for Simon-Hⁿ-a.e. x ∉ A_K,
 Θ*ⁿ(ν̂, A_K, x) = limsup_{ρ↓0} ν̂(A_K ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) / (ω_n · ofReal(ρ)ⁿ) = 0, where ω_n = realUnitBallVolume n ∈ (0, ∞).
 Simon's Hausdorff measure `simonHausdorffMeasureReal n` equals μHE[n] (SimonGMT `Chapter02.simonHausdorffMeasureReal_nat_eq_euclideanHausdorffMeasure`), so the exceptional set E_K := {x ∉ A_K : Θ*ⁿ(ν̂, A_K, x) ≠ 0} is μ-null.

5. (A good point.) Let Z := (S′ ∖ S) ∪ ⋃_{K∈𝒦} E_K, a countable union of μ-null sets, so μ(Z) = 0. Let y ∈ W with y ∉ S and y ∉ Z. Then y ∉ S′. Choose K ∈ 𝒦 with y ∈ interior K (step 3); then y ∉ A_K and y ∉ E_K, so limsup_{ρ↓0} ν(A_K ∩ B̄_ρ(y))/(ω_n ofReal(ρ)ⁿ) = 0 (ν̂ = ν on Borel sets). For ρ > 0 so small that B̄_ρ(y) ⊆ K we have A_K ∩ B̄_ρ(y) = S′ ∩ B̄_ρ(y), and ν(S′ ∩ B̄_ρ(y)) = ν(B̄_ρ(y)) by step 2.

6. (Conclusion.) Hence the [0, ∞]-valued function ρ ↦ ν(B̄_ρ(y))/(ω_n ofReal(ρ)ⁿ) has limsup 0 as ρ → 0+, so it tends to 0 (it is ≥ 0). Since the SimonGMT quotient uses ofReal(ρ)^(n : ℝ) = ofReal(ρ)ⁿ (`ENNReal.rpow_natCast`), ofReal(ρⁿ) = ofReal(ρ)ⁿ for ρ ≥ 0 (`ENNReal.ofReal_pow`), and ω_n is finite, ν(B̄_ρ(y))/ofReal(ρⁿ) = ω_n · [ν(B̄_ρ(y))/(ω_n ofReal(ρ)ⁿ)] → ω_n · 0 = 0. By step 1, ν(B̄_ρ(y)) = ∫⁻_{S∩B̄_ρ(y)} g dμ. This holds for every y ∈ W ∖ (S ∪ Z), i.e. for μ-a.e. y with y ∈ W and y ∉ S. ∎ (For n = 0 the same argument applies; then μ-null sets are empty and the statement says ν(B̄_ρ(y)) → ν({y}) = 0 for every y ∈ W ∖ S.)

Cover W by countably many compact balls K ⊆ W whose interiors cover W.
Apply Simon's Upper Density Theorem 3.6 (SimonGMT simon_theorem_3_6) to ν̂ = ν.toOuterMeasure (Borel regular) and A_K = S′ ∩ K; Simon's Hⁿ equals μHE[n], so exceptional sets are Hⁿ-null.
At y ∈ W∖(S ∪ null set), localize to B̄_ρ(y) ⊆ K: ν(A_K ∩ B̄_ρ(y)) = ν(B̄_ρ(y)), so the density quotient tends to 0; rescale by ω_n.

This is the boundedness part of Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(3) (the remark at the end of item 0(e) of the parent proof). It uses the sibling result
 (BLOWUP) for r′ > 0, any S and any g: ∫_{η_{y,r′}(S)} g dHⁿ = (r′ⁿ)⁻¹ ∫_S g(η_{y,r′}(x)) dHⁿ(x).
Let μ := μHE[n] on ℝ^Q and fix r > 0 with μ(S ∩ B̄_r(y)) < ∞.

1. (A cut-off function.) Let φ₀(z) := min(1, max(0, 2 − |z|)). Then φ₀ is continuous, 0 ≤ φ₀ ≤ 1, φ₀ = 1 on B̄_1(0) and φ₀ = 0 outside B̄_2(0); so φ₀ has compact support and defines an element of C_c(ℝ^Q, ℝ). Put L₀ := ∫_T φ₀ dHⁿ, a real number with L₀ ≥ 0 (φ₀ ≥ 0).

2. (Convergence.) By the tangent hypothesis, ∫_{η_{y,ρ}(S)} φ₀ dHⁿ → L₀ as ρ → 0+, so there is ρ₁ > 0 with ∫_{η_{y,ρ}(S)} φ₀ dHⁿ ≤ L₀ + 1 for all 0 < ρ < ρ₁.

3. (Comparison.) Let 0 < ρ < min(ρ₁, r/2). By (BLOWUP), ∫_{η_{y,ρ}(S)} φ₀ dHⁿ = (ρⁿ)⁻¹ ∫_S ψ dμ with ψ(x) := φ₀(η_{y,ρ}(x)) = φ₀(ρ⁻¹(x − y)). ψ is continuous, 0 ≤ ψ ≤ 1, ψ = 1 on B̄_ρ(y) and ψ = 0 outside B̄_{2ρ}(y). As 1_{B̄_ρ(y)} ≤ ψ pointwise,

4. (Conclusion.) Because μ(S ∩ B̄_ρ(y)) < ∞, step 3 gives μ(S ∩ B̄_ρ(y)) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal((L₀ + 1)ρⁿ) = (L₀ + 1) · ENNReal.ofReal(ρⁿ) (`ENNReal.ofReal_mul`, L₀ + 1 ≥ 0). Put K := L₀ + 1 ∈ ℝ≥0. The inequality μ(S ∩ B̄_ρ(y)) ≤ K · ENNReal.ofReal(ρⁿ) holds for all ρ ∈ (0, min(ρ₁, r/2)), a set belonging to 𝓝[>]0; i.e. it holds eventually as ρ → 0+. ∎
proof_key_steps: Take the cut-off φ₀ ∈ C_c with 1_{B̄_1(0)} ≤ φ₀ ≤ 1_{B̄_2(0)}; its blow-up integrals converge to L₀ = ∫_T φ₀, so are ≤ L₀ + 1 for small ρ.
BLOWUP: ∫_{η_{y,ρ}(S)} φ₀ = ρ^{−n} ∫_S φ₀∘η_{y,ρ}; for 2ρ < r the integrand is integrable on S and dominates 1_{B̄_ρ(y)}.
Hence Hⁿ(S ∩ B̄_ρ(y)) ≤ (L₀ + 1)ρⁿ for all small ρ; K := L₀ + 1.

 (BLOWUP) for λ > 0, any S and any g: ∫_{η_{y,λ}(S)} g dHⁿ = (λⁿ)⁻¹ ∫_S g(η_{y,λ}(x)) dHⁿ(x).
Let μ := μHE[n] on ℝ^Q.

1. (Dimension.) finrank T = n is part of the hypothesis that T is the approximate tangent space of N at y.

2. (Set-up.) Fix φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^Q, ℝ); choose R > 0 with tsupport φ ⊆ B̄_R(0) and put A := sup|φ|. For ρ > 0 let q₁(ρ) := μ((C ∖ N) ∩ B̄_ρ(y))/ofReal(ρⁿ) and q₂(ρ) := μ((N ∖ C) ∩ B̄_ρ(y))/ofReal(ρⁿ) in [0, ∞]. The map λ ↦ λR tends to 0 within (0, ∞) as λ → 0+, so by hypothesis q₁(λR) → 0 and q₂(λR) → 0 as λ → 0+.
